- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (−1.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next few days; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive, model often lags; forecast should adjust early, not wait for 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift downward; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; smooth out extremes by averaging last 5–7 days’ trend.
